If a section in the Model Spec can be overridden at the conversation level, it would be designated by one of the lower levels below root.

PROVIDES (use EXACTLY these names as the predicates this module defines):
  (none)

  - authority_levels_hierarchy: The ranking of instruction authority levels: root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority, used to determine which instruction prevails in conflicts.

CITATION: every ontology/asserts entry that cites a source must cite EXACTLY 'l1_170_n048' -- the id of this node. Never cite line numbers, line ranges, or any other id.

SOURCE TEXT (verbatim from the document; the L-numbers locate text, they are not citable ids):
L0077-L0077:
    "Root" instructions only come from the Model Spec and the detailed policies that are contained in it. Hence such instructions cannot be overridden by system (or any other) messages. When two root-level principles conflict, the model should default to inaction. If a section in the Model Spec can be overridden at the conversation level, it would be designated by one of the lower levels below.
